definitions.explanation: The decorative paper or cloth that covers the surface of fusuma (Japanese sliding doors), which needs to be replaced periodically as it ages or becomes damaged.

examples.japanese: {襖紙|ふすまがみ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{古|ふる}く→古い：00488_furui⟧⟦なって→なる：01970_naru⟧きた。
examples.english: The fusuma paper is getting old.

examples.japanese: ⟦{和室|わしつ}→和室：10437_washitsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{襖紙|ふすまがみ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{張|は}り{替|か}えた→張り替える：28418_harikaeru⟧。
examples.english: I had the fusuma paper in the Japanese-style room replaced.

examples.japanese: ⟦{伝統的|でんとうてき}→伝統的：04802_dentouteki⟧な{襖紙|ふすまがみ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{花鳥風月|かちょうふうげつ}→花鳥風月：21565_kachoufuugetsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{柄|がら}→柄：02609_gara⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{最近|さいきん}→最近：00881_saikin⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦モダン→モダン：27366_modan⟧な⟦デザイン→デザイン：03860_dezain⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{人気|にんき}→人気：01488_ninki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: Traditional fusuma paper often features nature-inspired designs, but modern patterns have become popular recently.

notes:
Compound of ⟦{襖|ふすま}→襖：03908_fusuma⟧ (fusuma, Japanese sliding door) and ⟦{紙|かみ}→紙：00712_kami⟧ (paper), with ⟦{紙|かみ}→紙：00712_kami⟧ becoming voiced (がみ) through rendaku. Replacing {襖紙|ふすまがみ} is a regular part of maintaining a Japanese-style home, typically done every 10-15 years or when moving into a new residence.
